resources.string: Today, a calendar and a board for your tasks. Choose where Helm keeps your plan; you can change it later in Settings.
No account and no server. Your plan stays on this phone, reminders and the morning summary included. Back it up to a file in Settings → Data.
Your own Helm server keeps the plan in sync with your other devices and lets AI agents work with it. On your computer run hlm pair and type the code it shows.
Replace the plan on this phone?
This phone holds the plan of %1$s. Connecting to %2$s replaces it with the plan there and removes %3$s from this phone. What reached %1$s stays there.
%1$s not sent to %2$s yet will be lost.
To keep them, save a backup first (Settings → Data → Backup) or connect to %1$s again.
The plan is kept on this phone and nothing is sent anywhere.
Last connected to %1$s. Changes made since then go there when you connect to it again.

A server of your own keeps Helm in sync across your devices and lets AI agents read and change the plan. Set one up as described at github.com/maiarowsky/helm (docs/deploy.md), run hlm pair on your computer and connect with the code. Everything on this phone then goes to the server.
The server\'s time zone decides what today is and when reminders ring.
No backup made on this phone yet

A backup is the whole plan on this phone in Helm\'s JSON format: tasks with their checklists, reminders and repeat rules, and the settings, without the change history. Helm does not copy your plan to Google or anywhere else, so keep the file somewhere safe. A Helm server reads it too (hlm import).
This file is not a Helm backup (Helm\'s JSON export, version 1).
The file has more than %1$d tasks; Helm restores at most %1$d at once.
These are sample tasks to show what Helm can do.
